title: Adaptive ingest summarizer and lineage tokens for high-cardinality Loki/ELK
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add an adaptive summarization layer to the log ingestion pipeline that produces compact semantic summaries and lineage tokens while preserving correlation IDs. The goal is to reduce storage and index pressure for high-cardinality sources (bursting debug traces, high-cardinality request metadata) while keeping traceability and debugability via a lightweight lineage token and deterministic fingerprint. The feature must support both Loki stream writes and Elasticsearch/Opensearch indices, be compatible with existing prefix/KV cache systems, and include an opt-out header for customers that require raw logs.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest summarizer deploys as a sidecar/ingest-stage and can be toggled via route config
Summarized payloads include a lineage_token, original_correlation_id (if present), and an irreversible summary field without raw sensitive fields
End-to-end latency added by summarizer < 15ms p95 at normal ingest rates and < 40ms during spikes
Storage reduction >= 35% for identified high-cardinality sources in 7-day sample workload
Loki streams accept summarized entries with consistent labels and a lineage_token that maps back to raw entries via a bounded TTL lookup table
Elasticsearch indices schema includes summary and lineage_token and queries by correlation_id still return either raw or summarized results depending on route configuration
Automated migration runbook to backfill/rehydrate summaries to raw if debug mode is enabled
Security review completed for PII redaction heuristics and KMS/HSM compatibility documented
design_notes: We will perform summarization with a deterministic semantic fingerprint: hashing canonicalized JSON after field allowlist/denylist and stable key ordering
Lineage_token format: v1:<base36(timestamp)>:<short-fingerprint> to be small and index-friendly
Correlation ID passthrough: preserve original trace/corr ids when present; generate best-effort correlation on noisy sources and mark with correlation_quality tag
Backpressure behavior: if summarizer queue depth crosses threshold, stream a lightweight stub entry (metadata-only) and emit a sampling signal for downstream reingestion
Privacy: summarizer will run an anonymization pass before summary generation using configured regex/pattern rules and optional KMS wrapped tokenization for sensitive fields
Compatibility: Loki path will write summarized entries into a companion stream with label summarized=true; ES path will write a summarized document into a separate index alias 'logs-summarized-*'
Tradeoffs: Summaries improve storage and query latency for aggregated views but make full-text debugging harder; lineage_token+lookup TTL mitigates this for short-term investigations

Integrate summarizer into ingest router with feature flag and route-level config
Add Loki companion stream writer and ES summarized index writer in ingest mapper
E2E benchmarking: synthetic workload to measure p95 latency and storage savings (scripts in infra/benchmarks/summary-test)
Security review: run PII heuristics and KMS integration review with security team
Create migration/backfill runbook and API to rehydrate raw logs from short-term raw buffer
Instrument observability: dashboards for summarizer latency, queue depth, summary_rate, rehydrate_requests
QA: chaos test under spikes, verify correlation chaining and lineage lookups
